messages.subject: terminate after serving request
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

Sometimes I know that a particular request is going to use up a lot of memory. I'd like the process to kill itself after it finishes serving so that apache will spin up a new, smaller process.

I noticed that php has a function that a process can call to register the process for termination.

http://php.net/manual/en/function.apache-child-terminate.php

Is there anything way to do this in Rapache?

Thanks,

Brad

messages.subject: Re: terminate after serving request
messages.body_plain:
I had trouble with the forking because STDOUT of the child process was not being sent as part of the HTTP response. I went back to the original idea of having the process kill itself.

Inside apache prefork (at least my setup!) sending a worker process the SIGUSR1 signal does exactly what I am asking---it tells the process to continue serving the current request and then kill itself. It takes another minute or so to die after but it works. The parent process will then spin off a new process.

So the trick is that when the process decides it is going to bloat itself it can send itself SIGUSR1. There is a pskill function in the R package "tools" to send a signal.

Here is an example script:

> library(tools)
> setContentType("text/html")
> cat("<pre>\n")
> pid <- Sys.getpid()
> cat("My process ID is ", pid, "\n")
>
> pskill(pid, signal = SIGUSR1)
>
> cat("Some text after sending the signal\n")
>
> OK

Now if I run it in rapache (i.e. open the page in my browser) I can monitor the apache jobs like this (friedmab is my account name on the server):

Before I open the page (the process IDs are in the 4th column: 14083 and 15159 are the workers and 32198 is the parent):

friedmab@rescomp232:~> ps -eadlf | grep httpd | grep friedmab | grep -v grep
1 S friedmab 14083 32198  0  80   0 - 55344 -      15:00 ?        00:00:00 /usr/sbin/httpd2-prefork -f /gne/home/friedmab/servers/test/conf/httpd.conf -k start
1 S friedmab 15159 32198  0  80   0 - 55344 -      15:01 ?        00:00:00 /usr/sbin/httpd2-prefork -f /gne/home/friedmab/servers/test/conf/httpd.conf -k start
1 S friedmab 32198     1  0  80   0 - 44061 -      12:19 ?        00:00:00 /usr/sbin/httpd2-prefork -f /gne/home/friedmab/servers/test/conf/httpd.conf -k start

This is the result seen in the browser:

> My process ID is  14083
> Some text after sending the signal

These are the processes a moment after the browser page is finished (14083 is still running):

friedmab@rescomp232:~> ps -eadlf | grep httpd | grep friedmab | grep -v grep
1 S friedmab  3265 32198  4  80   0 - 55344 -      15:11 ?        00:00:00 /usr/sbin/httpd2-prefork -f /gne/home/friedmab/servers/test/conf/httpd.conf -k start
1 S friedmab 14083 32198  0  80   0 - 56064 -      15:00 ?        00:00:00 /usr/sbin/httpd2-prefork -f /gne/home/friedmab/servers/test/conf/httpd.conf -k start
1 S friedmab 15159 32198  0  80   0 - 55344 -      15:01 ?        00:00:00 /usr/sbin/httpd2-prefork -f /gne/home/friedmab/servers/test/conf/httpd.conf -k start
1 S friedmab 32198     1  0  80   0 - 44061 -      12:19 ?        00:00:00 /usr/sbin/httpd2-prefork -f /gne/home/friedmab/servers/test/conf/httpd.conf -k start

Finally about 30 seconds later these are the processes:

friedmab@rescomp232:~> ps -eadlf | grep httpd | grep friedmab | grep -v grep
1 S friedmab  3265 32198  0  80   0 - 55344 -      15:11 ?        00:00:00 /usr/sbin/httpd2-prefork -f /gne/home/friedmab/servers/test/conf/httpd.conf -k start
1 S friedmab 15159 32198  0  80   0 - 55344 -      15:01 ?        00:00:00 /usr/sbin/httpd2-prefork -f /gne/home/friedmab/servers/test/conf/httpd.conf -k start
1 S friedmab 32198     1  0  80   0 - 44061 -      12:19 ?        00:00:00 /usr/sbin/httpd2-prefork -f /gne/home/friedmab/servers/test/conf/httpd.conf -k start

14083 has been killed...but only after finishing serving my page.
